observed: Both original FIFO publications had actual live and baseline replay receipts before the treatment change. Both keys were initially configured with identical owner/publisher and SNS service grants.

The sole treatment change added an explicit unconditional sns.amazonaws.com kms:Decrypt Deny. The CMK remained Enabled in every experimental DescribeKey control; no DisableKey or EnableKey was called. The original owner/publisher grant was unchanged, and a direct caller Encrypt/Decrypt control succeeded under the denied policy.

After the recorded approximately twenty-minute separation, the treatment fresh replay request reported Pending then Completed and received no original message during its approximately 91-second measured receive/status window. The independent same-age allowed archive replayed its exact original message to its own fresh queue and reported Completed.

Removing only the treatment service Decrypt Deny, with the same original Enabled CMK and unchanged topic/archive/message, allowed a fresh subscription and destination queue to receive that exact original MessageId and body with Replayed=true. The previously denied request remained Completed at the final status read; this does not demonstrate retry or recovery of that prior request.

CloudTrail EventName=Decrypt captured successful AWSService/sns.amazonaws.com calls for the same-age allowed archive at 2026-09-23T02:08:20Z and the restored treatment archive at 2026-09-23T02:10:00Z. Their original key ARNs and topic encryption contexts match the corresponding original receipts. These are direct cold archive KMS authority evidence, not elapsed-time assumptions.

Five unique owned Decrypt events were captured: two publication-time IAMUser events invokedBy SNS, one direct IAMUser owner-control event, and two later AWSService SNS archive events. No failed owned Decrypt event was returned by either paginated EventName lookup.
conclusions.negative_attribution_limit: The Deny-only/Enabled-key boundary is isolated by the unchanged key state, preserved owner rights, independent same-age allowed receipt, and same-original recovery after removing only the service Deny. However, no failed service-principal Decrypt event was returned. The actual failed KMS request, native KMS error code and denied-request principal therefore remain directly unobserved; recovery and allowed-control successful service calls do not substitute for a missing denial event. Owning-account CloudTrail eventual consistency and cross-account failed-call visibility prevent absence from proving no denied call occurred.
limits: No exact SNS archive cache lifetime or cache representation is measured. The twenty-minute timer and fresh queues alone do not establish a cold miss.

The explicit service Deny suppressed a bounded replay while the key was Enabled, unlike the prior combined disable-plus-deny experiment. This is not a universal immediate-denial guarantee for warm archive reads.
Completed is the actual observed status, not proof of delivery; no Failed status is synthesized. Only Pending and Completed were observed in this run.
Only fresh replay requests were used for recovery; automatic recovery of the earlier Completed request was not demonstrated.
The experiment covers one region/account, two original messages and one isolated policy transition. No live HTTP, rotation, alias-retargeting or subscriber authorization experiment was performed.

experiment_design: Two same-age isolated encrypted FIFO archives, initially identical documented grants and actual baseline replays. Add only explicit sns.amazonaws.com kms:Decrypt Deny to the treatment key, preserving owner/publisher rights. Both original keys stay Enabled until final cleanup. Fresh standard SQS queues and subscriptions avoid consumer deduplication. After twenty minutes, request both original replays and capture actual receipts/status. Remove only the treatment service Deny, request fresh original recovery, and correlate EventName=Decrypt CloudTrail events using exact owned resources. Elapsed time never establishes a cache miss.
limitations: Bounded receive absence is not a native Failed status or universal timeout.
Fresh queues do not guarantee a fresh SNS archive cache.
CloudTrail event history is eventually consistent and missing failed calls cannot prove they did not occur.
An allowed independent same-age archive is a scheduling control, not proof of the treatment cache state.
Only owned topics, subscriptions, queues and two tagged customer-managed keys are created; keys remain PendingDeletion for seven days.
redaction_note: CloudTrail events retain all native fields except accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken and confirmationToken values are replaced with [REDACTED]. Unrelated account events are omitted with counts; matching CloudTrailEvent JSON is reserialized. No new credentials are created.
